job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

response.passage: In our Class 6 science project, Mr. Sharma asked us to observe how water moves through different materials. We used three clear plastic cups and labeled them A, B, and C. For the experiment, we placed sand in cup A, clay in cup B, and gravel in cup C. On October 12th, Rahul poured 50 milliliters of water into each cup at exactly 9:00 AM. We noticed that the water drained quickly through the gravel because the large gaps between the stones allowed it to pass through easily. However, the clay held the water because its tiny particles are packed very tightly together. Priya, who lives in Delhi, noted that the water level in cup B did not drop at all after ten minutes. This activity showed us that the size of the particles determines how fast water moves through the ground. By 9:15 AM, the experiment was complete, and we recorded our findings in our notebooks. We learned that soil composition is vital for understanding how groundwater is stored beneath our feet.
response.summary: Students conducted an experiment using sand, clay, and gravel to observe water drainage. They discovered that particle size directly affects how quickly water passes through different types of soil.
